newsitem.title: USA: CSCE March world sugar ends barely up, trade buys.
newsitem.headline: CSCE March world sugar ends barely up, trade buys.

text.p: March CSCE world sugar futures clung what little gains they were able to make in early trade to close barely firmer, buoyed by light trade buying, dealers said.
Activity was constrained as players remained reluctant to make a definitive move after the market's recent plunge to one-month lows.
A 30-minute fire drill in the New York commodity exchanges that began at 1200 EST/1700 GMT, also dampened enthusiasm, floor sources said.
And when prices failed to retrace losses, the funds continued to sell, countering buying by the trade.
Today's volume reached 12,974 lots, with the bulk of contracts changing hands early in the session.
March closed 0.03 higher at 10.30 cents, setting its 10.35 to 10.26 trading range before midday. The back months finished 0.01 higher to 0.01 lower.

Tuesday's selloff pressured spot-March to its lowest level since Nov 6. While market sources agree losses were the result of mainly technical factors, and the market is oversold based on the charts, an unbalanced world supply and demand picture continues to weigh heavily on prices, they said.
